title: Remote Sensing Scientists and Technologists
description: Apply remote sensing principles and methods to analyze data and solve problems in areas such as natural resource management, urban planning, or homeland security. May develop new sensor systems, analytical techniques, or new applications for existing systems.

tasks.text: Manage or analyze data obtained from remote sensing systems to obtain meaningful results.
Analyze data acquired from aircraft, satellites, or ground-based platforms, using statistical analysis software, image analysis software, or Geographic Information Systems (GIS).
Integrate other geospatial data sources into projects.
Organize and maintain geospatial data and associated documentation.
Compile and format image data to increase its usefulness.
Prepare or deliver reports or presentations of geospatial project information.
Discuss project goals, equipment requirements, or methodologies with colleagues or team members.
Process aerial or satellite imagery to create products such as land cover maps.
Design or implement strategies for collection, analysis, or display of geographic data.
Develop or build databases for remote sensing or related geospatial project information.
Collect supporting data, such as climatic or field survey data, to corroborate remote sensing data analyses.
Monitor quality of remote sensing data collection operations to determine if procedural or equipment changes are necessary.
Train technicians in the use of remote sensing technology.
Set up or maintain remote sensing data collection systems.
Direct all activity associated with implementation, operation, or enhancement of remote sensing hardware or software.
Attend meetings or seminars or read current literature to maintain knowledge of developments in the field of remote sensing.
Conduct research into the application or enhancement of remote sensing technology.
Recommend new remote sensing hardware or software acquisitions.
Use remote sensing data for forest or carbon tracking activities to assess the impact of environmental change.
Develop automated routines to correct for the presence of image distorting artifacts, such as ground vegetation.
Develop new analytical techniques or sensor systems.
Participate in fieldwork.
Apply remote sensing data or techniques, such as surface water modeling or dust cloud detection, to address environmental issues.
Direct installation or testing of new remote sensing hardware or software.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Science
skills.def: Using scientific rules and methods to solve problems.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Programming
skills.def: Writing computer programs for various purposes.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: C#, C++, Objective C, Oracle Java.

skills.name: Data base management system software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or provide access to a set of related information. Examples: Amazon DynamoDB, Apache Hadoop, Apache Hive, Elasticsearch.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: Apache Kafka, C, Go, Interface definition language IDL.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud EC2, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Web Services AWS software, Oracle Database.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Bash, Linux, Microsoft Windows, UNIX.

skills.name: Web platform development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications accessed through web sites or using web technologies such as HTML. Examples: Hypertext preprocessor PHP, JavaScript, JavaScript Object Notation JSON, Node.js.
